clips.caption: The speaker introduces the concept of a 'harness' as a system of tools, prompts, and skills, comparing it to a video game loadout, and emphasizes its importance in building AI agents.
The speaker introduces CT, a colleague with expertise in tokenomics and a skill called Even Better If, highlighting his contributions to efficient AI workflows.
CT shares his experience of hitting API usage limits, burning through tokens, and facing high costs, prompting a deep dive into optimizing AI usage.
CT explains how he developed 'Conductor,' a system to audit and optimize token usage by analyzing model selection, caching, and task routing.
The speaker outlines five key levers for cost control: model selection, caching, routing, task decomposition, and delegation to cheaper models.
CT details how he implemented a conductor system that delegates routine tasks to cheaper models like Haiku and Sonnet while reserving Fable 5 for high-level judgment.
The speaker introduces the EBI skill—'Even Better If'—a feedback loop for continuous improvement, which he integrated into his agent system for iterative refinement.
CT demonstrates how the EBI skill runs multiple rounds of feedback, identifying high-impact improvements and synthesizing actionable insights across projects.
The conductor system is described as cache-friendly and transparent, allowing real-time monitoring of agent transcripts and delegation processes.
CT reports up to 80% reduction in plan usage and 31% cost savings after implementing the conductor system, with sustained efficiency over time.
